chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is [the reward] for the one who performs Ziyarah of one of you?' He (peace be upon him) said: '[It is] as if he has performed Ziyarah of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَحَداً مِنْكُمْ: One of you (referring to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the theological principle that the Imams are the living continuation of the Prophet’s mission, making their visitation spiritually equivalent to visiting the Messenger himself. This equivalence reinforces the Shia concept of the Imams as the perfect exemplars of the Prophet’s character and authority, elevating Ziyarah from a mere social act to a profound spiritual obligation that mirrors the reverence due to the Prophet.
